name: Mechanical
placeholder: e.g. Bicycle gears, Door lock, Jet engine
guide: Teach mechanisms: parts, how they connect and move, forces, wear and failure.

name: Electromechanical & robotics
guide: Teach how motors, sensors, power electronics and control work together with the mechanics; for robots, cover sensing, deciding and acting.

name: Electrical & electronics
guide: Teach how electricity is generated, moved, stored, switched and controlled: the components, what each does, and why designs are chosen. Explain ideas like voltage and current in plain words, without calculations.

name: Civil engineering
guide: Teach how structures and infrastructure carry loads, resist nature (wind, water, earthquakes, soil) and are built and maintained — the structural idea first, then materials, construction and safety.

name: Software & coding
guide: Teach software as problem-solving: the idea, the data structures and algorithms, trade-offs, and how real systems scale. Describe approaches in plain words — no code or syntax required, though learners may use pseudocode.

name: Human body & medicine
guide: Teach the body as a set of solutions to needs (every cell needs oxygen; waste must be removed), and medical technology as engineering that supports or replaces those solutions. Educational only: no diagnosis, treatment or dosing advice, and nothing about making pathogens or toxins more dangerous.
